root_idea.summary: The root centers on nearness: being close, drawing near, or bringing something near. Its comparative extensions describe what is nearer, lower, less, or more suitable.
root_idea.development: Concrete spatial proximity extends to temporal, relational, and figurative closeness. The feminine comparative دُنْيَا develops the conventional sense of the present or nearer world, contrasted with the hereafter.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I citation form دَنَا.
Displayed under the normalized comparative citation form أَدْنَى.
Displayed under the active-participle citation form دَانٍ.
Displayed under the feminine active-participle citation form دَانِيَة.
Displayed as the established nominal citation form دُنْيَا.
The T-tagged occurrence is the same lexical comparative أَدْنَى and is represented under the same public form.

senses.usage_conditions: Used of physical, spatial, temporal, or otherwise apprehensible approach; the Quran includes an approach expressed without a direct object.

senses.definition: To bring or draw something near; to draw it down toward or over someone.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive construction; in the Quranic clothing expression, it denotes drawing part of an outer garment down over the body.

senses.definition: Nearer or nearest; closer in place, relation, time, or degree.
senses.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative adjective, opposed to أَقْصَى in spatial or relational comparison and used more broadly for what is closer.

senses.definition: More suitable, more apt, or more likely to achieve the intended result.
senses.usage_conditions: A figurative comparative of closeness: what is nearer to the desired or appropriate outcome.

senses.definition: Less or smaller in amount, number, or degree.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in comparison with what is greater or more; the Quran applies it to a lesser punishment and to a smaller amount of recitation.

senses.definition: Lower, inferior, worse, or of lesser worth.
senses.usage_conditions: Opposed to خير or to what is better; it may be substantivized for what is lower or inferior, including the lower worldly life.
Active participle of دَنَا; in the Quran it describes something brought near or hanging within reach.

senses.definition: Near, close, or hanging low within reach.
senses.usage_conditions: Feminine active participle of دَنَا; used of vegetation, fruit, or other things situated conveniently near.

senses.definition: The nearer, nearest, or lowest of two or more things.
senses.usage_conditions: The feminine comparative may be used attributively or substantively; in the Quran it describes the nearer bank and the nearest or lowest heaven.

senses.definition: The present world or worldly life, including its worldly enjoyments and prosperity.
senses.usage_conditions: A conventional noun contrasted with الْآخِرَةُ, the world to come; it may refer to the present state of existence or to its benefits.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be near in kinship; to be related or closely connected by family.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun دَنَاوَةٌ may denote kinship or close relationship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be weak, contemptible, ignoble, unprofitable, or deficient in what one undertakes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct adjective/verb branch from the root, describing low standing, weakness, or poor performance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bring words close together; in a reported eating directive, to eat what is nearest or immediately before one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the conventional directive to eat from what lies nearest to the eater.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pursue small, paltry, or contemptible matters.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived Form II usage concerning the choice or pursuit of mean or insignificant things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become weak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form II usage recorded as synonymous with ضَعُفَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw near to undertaking or experiencing an affair or event.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is an affair, event, or undertaking rather than a person or physical object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To tighten or contract a pair of hobbles; to bring two matters close together or make them connected.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used both of tightening the two parts of a camel's hobbles and of making events nearly continuous or connected.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be near to giving birth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized intransitive use applied to a pregnant woman or she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To live a strait or restricted life after ease and abundance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV usage describing a change from prosperity to constrained circumstances.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw near or approach gradually, little by little.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form V derivation emphasizes gradual progression toward nearness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw near to one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI construction with mutual subjects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw together or contract.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a thing or things becoming gathered, shortened, or contracted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a man's camels, to become few and weak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized collective use applied to a herd whose number or condition has diminished.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek, desire, or demand nearness; to seek to make someone approach or to cause someone to draw near.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form X construction may express either seeking nearness or causing another to approach.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Closely related or near in kinship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in kinship expressions such as a near paternal or maternal cousin or other close relation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Worldly; pertaining to the present world or present state of existence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational adjective formed from دُنْيَا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Near or closely attached; a close, sincere, or particular friend.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can denote either proximity or the closeness of a trusted personal relationship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weak or contemptible; of low standing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate adjectival branch from the sense of nearness; some authorities distinguish this form from دَنِىءٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A low or base quality, disposition, practice, or action; disgrace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a blameworthy condition or conduct, including what one would prefer death to endure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Former, first, foremost, or frontmost.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical comparative extension opposed to what is later, last, or farther behind; it can describe the forepart of an object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Near to giving birth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized active-participial use applied to a she-camel or a woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weak, contemptible, unprofitable, or falling short of what one ought to accomplish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived participial adjective describing deficient ability, worth, or performance.
